key_insight: ARGON decouples neutral-atom compilation into offline spatial layout design and online temporal routing, using a GNN to avoid future bottlenecks and scale beyond joint spatiotemporal search.
engineering_relevance: This framework makes large-scale neutral-atom quantum compilers faster and more practical by preserving hardware constraints while improving routing efficiency and execution fidelity.
method: Offline precompute hardware-certified, high-parallelism spatial layouts
Use a GNN to score candidate layouts against deep temporal dependencies
Apply a heuristic router to generate collision-free atom transport schedules
evidence_signal: The abstract reports compilation in under 10 seconds, up to >10^4x speedup versus baselines, and up to 10^2x fidelity improvement on dense circuits.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the precomputed layout library and the GNN’s ability to generalize to unseen circuit structures and hardware conditions.
paper_title: ARGON: A GNN-Empowered Compilation Framework for Scalable Neutral Atom Computing
